sentences.text: The only known specimen is a partial wing measuring 13 cm (5 inches) in length.
The bones of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — were found articulated but were badly crushed during fossilization.
After matrix removal in the 1970s, the bones were found to be very slender with little diagnostic detail and no similarity to modern Anatidae.
The genus Eonessa was first described by Alexander Wetmore in May 1938.
The holotype specimen was collected on August 26, 1936, from the Myton Pocket in Duchesne County, Utah, USA.
In 1978, Storrs Olson and Alan Feduccia removed Eonessa from the family Anatidae after restudying the holotype.
Olson and Feduccia classified Eonessa as Aves incertae sedis, suggesting it might belong to the order Gruiformes.
Eonessa belongs to the parent group Eonessinae.
Eonessa is classified within the family Anatidae.
Eonessa lived during the Middle Eocene, approximately 46 to 42 million years ago.
The time range for Eonessa spans from the Lutetian to the Bartonian stages, between 45.9 and 39.7 million years ago.
